title: Expectation builds confidence
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do your expectations of people do to them?
A student said: he inspires them, showing an unlimited approach and the possibilities. Giving people that decision turns them inward and makes them ask those questions.

Jose said: he expects unquestioned beliefs. A student said it probably builds confidence in people. Jose said: that is exactly what it does. It gives people confidence when you say: I will not accept external excuses, this year you will make the number, and we will talk about how.
Jose said that a relentless belief commands your nervous system and all the possibilities you have in the present and the future. He said the leader probably does it by accident, not by analysis.

groups.heading: A power move and a culture

lines.text: A student said: it also strikes me as a power play. He is letting people know he is in charge and things will be drastically different.
Jose said: I am not judging which culture was right. A leader who moves to another company changes its culture, because he has a system that he knows works.
A student said: the indirect instilling of confidence through the expectation is a powerful concept.
Jose said that in a long partnership you hold a positive belief about the person and endure hardships together. A student said: it is a choice to have a positive belief system.
What expectation could you state to someone so that it builds their confidence?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write an expectation you hold of someone.
Write how you could state it without an excuse.
Write how it could help them.
Write how it could pressure them.
Write how you would tell the difference.

check.q: What did Jose say an unquestioned expectation gives people?
What did a student say it could also be?
What did a student say about a positive belief system?

recap: State expectations that build confidence. Know the difference from pressure.
